case_name: Ga Arife @ Arti Sharma vs Gopal Dutt Sharma
facts_of_case: Appellant, a Muslim woman, challenged the orders of the Courts below. She sought to prove her conversion from Islam to Hinduism and lawfully marry the respondent according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to introduce a new plea to prove it by leading evidence.
legal_principles.held: Counsel for the respondent further argued that the appellant failed to disclose that in what manner and on the performance of which ceremonies and who are the pundits through whom she got herself converted to Hindu religion.
cited_cases: Gullipilli Sowria Raj vs Bandaru Pavani alias Gullipilli Pavani (2009) 1 SCC 714

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot introduce a new plea in the middle of proceedings without leading sufficient evidence to support it.
legal_principles.held: Counsel for the respondent further submitted that during the pendency of the said petition, the appellant had moved an application under Order 6 Rule 17 r/w Section 151 CPC to seek amendment in her divorce petition with a view to introduce the said plea of conversion but the same was disallowed by the matrimonial Court.

outcome.final_order: The crucial question was whether the appellant could successfully prove her conversion from Islam to Hinduism so as to lawfully marry the respondent according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
